question: Gearbox (remote-hijack a car) control scheme. Built: aim-to-steer, the hijacked car drives at 14 m/s toward the mouse reticle (turns at most 140 deg/s) for up to 6 s while Rivet stays on foot at 35% move speed (the cost). Measured: the car turns onto a robot 17 m off-axis and wrecks it in 1.42 s. Which control should Gearbox have?

options.label: Aim-to-steer (as built): the car follows the reticle until it crashes or 6 s end
options.tradeoff: skill-expressive and can thread traffic or chase a dodging enemy; Rivet is slowed and exposed while steering

options.label: Target-and-launch: lock an enemy, the car homes on it by itself
options.tradeoff: one click and Rivet keeps full speed and his gun; less skill, more a guided missile

options.label: Hybrid: steer while the button is held, release to launch straight at the last aim
options.tradeoff: both feels in one input; slightly harder to teach
